notes.front: What is Microsoft Power BI?
notes.back: A suite of Microsoft tools and services that data analysts use to build interactive data visualisations for business users.
notes.explanation: The training introduces it for enterprise-scale analytics, which often needs complex modelling, interactive reporting and secure sharing.
notes.example: Like a newspaper’s graphics desk that turns raw figures into charts readers can click into, but working on a company’s own data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Power BI Desktop?
notes.back: A Windows application for importing data, organising it into an analytics model and creating interactive reports.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s overview describes Desktop as the best place for data modelling and report creation.
notes.example: Like an architect’s drawing office, where the plans are drafted and checked before anyone else sees them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Power BI service?
notes.back: Power BI’s cloud service, where reports are published and then used by business users.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s overview calls it the cloud platform for publishing, sharing and collaboration.
notes.example: Like a gallery that hangs the architect’s finished plans where visitors can walk round them and ask questions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Power BI and Fabric, what is a semantic model?
notes.back: A model built from related tables that sets out the numeric values to analyse and the entities to group them by.
notes.explanation: The training says the general term is an analytical model; Fabric and Power BI call it a semantic model.
notes.example: Like the rules of a sports league table, which fix which scores are added up and how teams are grouped, so every reader gets the same totals.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Describe core concepts of data modeling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a semantic model, what is a measure?
notes.back: A numeric value you want to analyse or report on, such as revenue or quantity sold.
notes.explanation: Measures are aggregated across dimensions, for example to find total revenue by customer.
notes.example: Like the runs in a cricket scorebook: the numbers you add up and compare.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Describe core concepts of data modeling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a semantic model, what is a dimension?
notes.back: An entity you use to aggregate measures by, such as product, customer or time.
notes.explanation: Dimensions let you ask questions such as total items sold by product in each month.
notes.example: Like the headings you group a cricket scorebook by: batter, match or season.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Describe core concepts of data modeling”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Power BI service, what is a report?
notes.back: One or more pages of interactive visuals, text and graphics, all based on a single semantic model.
notes.explanation: Its pages are often organised around particular questions or areas of interest.
notes.example: Like an annual report whose charts you can click to filter, with every page drawing on the same set of accounts.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, Power BI service basics, “Key Power BI service concepts and terms”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Power BI service, what is a dashboard?
notes.back: A single screen of tiles holding interactive visuals, text and graphics.
notes.explanation: Dashboards are often used to monitor metrics or to tell a story.
notes.example: Like a car’s instrument panel: one glance shows the few readings that matter most.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, Power BI service basics, “Key Power BI service concepts and terms”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Power BI mobile app for?
notes.back: Viewing and using Power BI reports and dashboards on phones and tablets.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s overview describes it as optimised for phones and tablets, for viewing reports on the go.
notes.example: Like a pocket edition of a guidebook: the same content, sized for reading on the move.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, What is Power BI?, “Power BI Desktop vs. the Power BI service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Power BI and Fabric, what is a workspace?
notes.back: A shared, collaborative area where teams store and manage reports, dashboards, semantic models and other Fabric items.
notes.explanation: Business users are given roles in a workspace that control what they can see and do.
notes.example: Like a shared project room with key cards: everyone works on the same boards, but not everyone may move them.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, Power BI service basics, “Key Power BI service concepts and terms”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a star schema, what is a fact table?
notes.back: A table storing observations or events, such as sales orders, with numeric measure columns and key columns linking to dimensions.
notes.explanation: Its dimension key columns set its dimensionality, while the key values set its granularity.
notes.example: Like a shop’s till roll: one line per sale, with the amount and codes pointing to the product and the cashier.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Fact tables”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a star schema, what is a dimension table?
notes.back: A table describing a business entity, such as products, people or places, with a key column that uniquely identifies each row.
notes.explanation: Its other columns are there to support filtering and grouping the data.
notes.example: Like a staff directory: one row per person, used to look people up and group them by team.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Dimension tables”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a star schema?
notes.back: A mature modelling approach, widely used in relational data warehouses, that classes every model table as either a dimension or a fact.
notes.explanation: In the training’s terms, it is the design in which a fact table relates to one or more dimension tables.
notes.example: Like a hub airport with routes going straight out to each destination and none between the destinations.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Star schema overview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a snowflake schema?
notes.back: A design in which dimension tables relate to further detail tables, for example a Region table linked to a Store table.
notes.explanation: The training’s own example links a Category table to a Product table.
notes.example: Like a river delta, where each channel from the main stream splits again into smaller ones.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a semantic model, what is a hierarchy?
notes.back: An arrangement of a dimension’s levels, such as products under categories, used to move between levels of aggregation.
notes.explanation: A Customer table might, for instance, group customers by city.
notes.example: Like a postal address: country, then town, then street, then house number.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Attribute hierarchies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Power BI, what do drill down and drill up mean?
notes.back: Moving through a hierarchy to a more detailed level (down) or to a more summarised level (up).
notes.explanation: For example, you might view total sales by year and then drill down to see each month.
notes.example: Like zooming a map in from country to city, and back out again.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Attribute hierarchies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the VertiPaq engine in Power BI?
notes.back: The efficient, in-memory columnar store in which Power BI keeps data loaded into a semantic model.
notes.explanation: Aggregations are worked out at query time, giving fast analysis and reporting.
notes.example: Like a card index filed by column rather than by row, so totting up one column means opening just one drawer.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Model view in Power BI Desktop?
notes.back: The view where you shape a semantic model: relationships between tables, hierarchies, data types and display formats.
notes.explanation: It is where fact and dimension tables are linked together, along with other properties that shape the model for analysis.
notes.example: Like the floor-plan view in a home-design program, where you connect rooms rather than decorate them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Analytical modeling in Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Direct Lake?
notes.back: A Power BI semantic model storage mode in Fabric, ideal for models over large lakehouses, warehouses and other sources with Delta tables.
notes.explanation: It is especially useful when copying the entire data volume into an Import table is impractical or impossible.
notes.example: Like a reading room that fetches only the pages you ask for from the archive, instead of photocopying the whole archive first.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Direct Lake is ideal for semantic models connecting to large Fabric lakehouses, warehouses, and other Fabric data sources with Delta tables. Direct Lake is especially useful when replicating the entire data volume into an Import table is impractical or impossible.

notes.front: In Power BI, what is a card visual?
notes.back: A visual that shows a single value, useful for highlighting an important figure or metric.
notes.explanation: Tables and text, cards included, are often the simplest way to communicate data.
notes.example: Like the large “days without an accident” sign at a factory gate.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Tables and text”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a DAX measure?
notes.back: A measure defined by a formula written in DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) that summarises data.
notes.explanation: Such formulas often use aggregation functions like sum, minimum, maximum and average, and the values are calculated at query time rather than stored.
notes.example: Like a spreadsheet total that recalculates itself for whatever filter a reader chooses.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Measures”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Copilot in Power BI?
notes.back: An AI assistant built into Power BI that helps you create reports, analyse data and produce natural-language summaries.
notes.explanation: It is switched on by default, but it needs a paid capacity.
notes.example: Like an assistant who drafts report pages and a summary from your brief, which you then check.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, Power BI service basics, “Key Power BI service concepts and terms”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where does a typical Power BI workflow begin?
notes.back: In Power BI Desktop: importing and combining data into a model, then creating reports.
notes.explanation: Desktop can import data from a wide range of sources before organising it into an analytics model.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After creating models and reports in Power BI Desktop, what is the next step in the typical workflow?
notes.back: Publishing them to the Power BI service.
notes.explanation: Business users then interact with the published reports there, in a browser or on mobile devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two things you can do in the Power BI service besides viewing reports?
notes.back: Any two of: schedule refreshes of data sources, share reports with others, define dashboards and apps.
notes.explanation: Users can then consume the reports, dashboards and apps in a browser or on mobile devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Power BI is a core workload of which Microsoft platform?
notes.back: Microsoft Fabric.
notes.explanation: Within Fabric, Power BI content sits in shared workspaces alongside data engineering items, all backed by OneLake.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Power BI in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: On which operating system does Power BI Desktop run?
notes.back: Microsoft Windows.
notes.explanation: The training calls Desktop a Microsoft Windows application, and it is where the typical Power BI workflow starts.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Fabric, how many reports can a single semantic model serve?
notes.back: Several: one semantic model can be shared across multiple reports.
notes.explanation: The training lists shareable semantic models among the Fabric-specific capabilities of Power BI.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Power BI in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides measures, what two things does a semantic model define for the reports built on it?
notes.back: Relationships and hierarchies.
notes.explanation: The training lists measures, relationships and hierarchies together as what reports are built on.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Power BI in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two things Copilot in Power BI can do?
notes.back: Any two of: summarise a report in plain language, create report pages, generate DAX measures.
notes.explanation: The training says these abilities are available in both Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Copilot in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Copilot in Power BI needs a paid capacity: Microsoft Fabric {{c1::`F2`}} or higher, or Power BI Premium `P1` or higher.
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s service basics page gives the same thresholds and notes that Copilot is on by default.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Copilot in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Power BI AI feature works without a Copilot licence and writes a text summary of what a report’s data shows?
notes.back: The smart narrative visual.
notes.explanation: Its summary updates dynamically as the data changes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Other AI features”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a fact table, what does each row represent?
notes.back: A recorded event, such as one sales transaction with its quantity and revenue.
notes.explanation: Fact tables hold the numeric measures that the model is built to analyse.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a dimension table, what does every row have besides its attribute columns?
notes.back: A unique key value.
notes.explanation: The other columns hold attributes such as product names, categories or customer cities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Most analytical models include a {{c1::time}} dimension, so measures can be aggregated across periods.
notes.back: time
notes.explanation: Microsoft’s star schema guidance likewise calls a date dimension table the most consistent table you will find in a star schema.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How might a hierarchy in a Time table be arranged?
notes.back: Days grouped into months, and months grouped into years.
notes.explanation: Each level gives another grain at which measures can be aggregated.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Attribute hierarchies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a Power BI semantic model, which table type enables filtering and grouping, and which enables summarisation?
notes.back: Dimension tables enable filtering and grouping; fact tables enable summarisation.
notes.explanation: Each report visual sends a query that generally filters, groups and summarises model data, which fits this division.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Star schema relevance to Power BI semantic models”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a one-to-many model relationship, which side is the dimension table?
notes.back: The “one” side; the “many” side is the fact table.
notes.explanation: No table property marks a table as dimension or fact; the relationship’s cardinality decides it.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Star schema relevance to Power BI semantic models”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two drawbacks of mimicking a snowflake dimension design in Power BI?
notes.back: Any two of: more tables to load, longer filter propagation chains, a less intuitive Data pane.
notes.explanation: The guidance also notes that a hierarchy cannot span columns from more than one table.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Snowflake dimensions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which engine processes Direct Lake queries, and how does their performance compare with Import mode?
notes.back: The VertiPaq engine; query performance is comparable to Import mode.
notes.explanation: Direct Lake gets this without the overhead of refresh cycles that load the entire data volume.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Similar to Import mode, Direct Lake queries are processed by the VertiPaq engine, and thus deliver query performance comparable to Import mode without the management overhead of data refresh cycles to load the entire data volume.

notes.front: What does a Direct Lake refresh copy, compared with an Import mode refresh?
notes.back: Only metadata, whereas Import mode replicates the data into an entire cached copy.
notes.explanation: Copying only metadata can take just a few seconds.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Import mode replicates the data and creates an entire cached copy of the data for the semantic model, whereas a Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata (known as framing, described later in this article), which can take a few seconds to complete.

notes.front: Can the data volume analysed through Direct Lake exceed the capacity’s maximum memory?
notes.back: Yes, because only the data needed to answer a query is loaded into memory.
notes.explanation: The documentation presents this as a way Direct Lake maximises return on investment.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Maximizes return on investment (ROI) because analyzed data volumes can exceed the capacity's max memory limits, since only the data that's needed to answer a query is loaded into memory.

notes.front: For which layer of the medallion architecture is Direct Lake described as an ideal choice?
notes.back: The gold analytics layer.
notes.explanation: Direct Lake builds on existing Fabric lakehouses and warehouses that hold Delta tables.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Uses existing Fabric investments by seamlessly integrating with large lakehouses, warehouses, and other Fabric sources with Delta tables. For example, Direct Lake is an ideal choice for the *gold* analytics layer in the medallion lakehouse architecture.

notes.front: When is a table the right way to show data in a report?
notes.back: When many related values need to be displayed.
notes.explanation: Tables and text are often the simplest way to communicate data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Tables and text”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of chart is a good way to compare numeric values across discrete categories?
notes.back: A bar or column chart.
notes.explanation: The training treats bar and column charts together for this job.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Bar and column charts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of chart is useful for examining trends, often over time?
notes.back: A line chart.
notes.explanation: Line charts can also compare categorised values.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Line charts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of chart compares categorised values as proportions of a total?
notes.back: A pie chart.
notes.explanation: The training notes these are often used in business reports.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Pie charts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which visual compares two numeric measures to find a relationship or correlation between them?
notes.back: A scatter plot.
notes.explanation: The training singles out relationships and correlations as what scatter plots help you spot.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Scatter plots”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which visual compares values for different geographic areas or locations?
notes.back: A map.
notes.explanation: The training lists maps among the common visualisations, alongside charts and tables.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Maps”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a Power BI report, what happens when you select a category in one visual?
notes.back: That category is automatically filtered and highlighted in the other related visuals in the report.
notes.explanation: Visuals for related data in a report are linked to one another automatically.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Interactive reports in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Power BI AI visual lets report users ask questions in plain English and get chart answers?
notes.back: The Q&A visual.
notes.explanation: Its answers are based on the semantic model behind the report.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “AI-driven visualizations in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Power BI AI visual identifies the factors that most strongly drive a selected metric?
notes.back: Key influencers.
notes.explanation: It shows its results as an interactive visual.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “AI-driven visualizations in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Power BI AI visual lets you drill down interactively across several dimensions to see what contributes to a value?
notes.back: The decomposition tree.
notes.explanation: It is one of four AI-powered visuals the training lists, with smart narratives, Q&A and key influencers.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “AI-driven visualizations in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An analyst has built a model and a report in Power BI Desktop on her laptop. Colleagues must now view and interact with it in a web browser. What should she do next?
notes.back: B: publish it to the Power BI service.
notes.choices:
A) Email the Desktop file to each colleague
B) Publish it to the Power BI service
C) Copy each visual into a card
D) Rebuild the report in the Power BI mobile app
notes.choicesExplained: A: colleagues would need Desktop and would not be using the shared service. D: the mobile app is for viewing, not building. C: cards show single values and do not share anything.
notes.explanation: The typical Power BI workflow builds in Desktop and then publishes to the service, where business users consume reports.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A modeller needs the full set of modelling and design tools to combine several data sources into a new model. Which should he use?
notes.back: D: Power BI Desktop.
notes.choices:
A) The Power BI mobile app
B) A card visual
C) A dashboard in the Power BI service
D) Power BI Desktop
notes.choicesExplained: A: the mobile app is for viewing. C: dashboards display tiles; browser editing is limited compared with Desktop. B: a card is a single visual, not a modelling tool.
notes.explanation: Desktop offers full data modelling and design tools, which is why it is the place to create reports.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, What is Power BI?, “Power BI Desktop vs. the Power BI service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A library model has a table with one row per branch library, holding a branch key, its name, town and region. Is it a fact table or a dimension table?
notes.back: A dimension table.
notes.explanation: It describes an entity with a unique key and attributes used for filtering and grouping, not recorded events.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The same model has a table with one row per book loan, holding the loan date, branch key, member key and any fine paid. Is it a fact table or a dimension table?
notes.back: A fact table.
notes.explanation: Each row records an event, with keys to dimensions and a numeric value (the fine) to summarise.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a model, the Loans fact table links to a Branch table, and the Branch table links on to a separate Region table. What is this design called?
notes.back: D: a snowflake schema.
notes.choices:
A) A star schema
B) A lambda architecture
C) A Direct Lake model
D) A snowflake schema
notes.choicesExplained: A: in a star schema, dimension tables relate only to the fact table. B: lambda is a batch and stream processing pattern. C: Direct Lake is a storage mode, not a table design.
notes.explanation: A dimension table (Branch) relating to a further detail table (Region) is what turns a star into a snowflake.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A manager looking at yearly membership totals wants to see the months within 2025. What should she do in the report?
notes.back: B: drill down through the Time hierarchy.
notes.choices:
A) Drill up to decades
B) Drill down through the Time hierarchy
C) Add a second fact table
D) Switch to the Power BI mobile app
notes.choicesExplained: A: drilling up gives less detail, not more. C: the months are already a level of the existing hierarchy. D: changing device does not change the level of detail.
notes.explanation: Moving from years to months is moving down one level of a hierarchy.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Attribute hierarchies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A Fabric lakehouse holds very large Delta tables. The team wants fast in-memory reporting without copying the whole data volume into an Import model on a refresh schedule. Which option fits?
notes.back: D: Direct Lake.
notes.choices:
A) Import mode with a scheduled full refresh
B) A Real-Time Dashboard
C) A Power BI dashboard pinned from a report
D) Direct Lake
notes.choicesExplained: A: this is exactly the full copy the team wants to avoid. B: a Real-Time Intelligence dashboard, not a semantic model storage mode. C: a dashboard still needs a semantic model behind it; it is not a storage mode.
notes.explanation: Direct Lake is ideal for large lakehouses with Delta tables, especially when replicating all the data into Import is impractical.
notes.source: Microsoft Fabric documentation (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs), Direct Lake overview, “Direct Lake overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · CC BY 4.0
notes.evidence: Direct Lake is ideal for semantic models connecting to large Fabric lakehouses, warehouses, and other Fabric data sources with Delta tables. Direct Lake is especially useful when replicating the entire data volume into an Import table is impractical or impossible.

notes.front: A charity wants to show how its monthly donations have risen and fallen over the last three years. Which visual fits best?
notes.back: C: a line chart.
notes.choices:
A) A pie chart
B) A map
C) A line chart
D) A card
notes.choicesExplained: A: a pie shows shares of a total, not change over time. B: a map compares places. D: a card shows a single figure.
notes.explanation: Line charts are the visual for examining trends over time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Line charts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A town council wants to show what share of its total budget each department receives. Which visual fits best?
notes.back: D: a pie chart.
notes.choices:
A) A scatter plot
B) A line chart
C) A map
D) A pie chart
notes.choicesExplained: A: a scatter plot relates two numeric measures. B: a line chart shows trends. C: a map compares geographic areas.
notes.explanation: Pie charts compare categorised values as proportions of a total.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Pie charts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An analyst wants to see whether shops that spend more on advertising also take more in sales. Which visual fits best?
notes.back: B: a scatter plot.
notes.choices:
A) A pie chart
B) A scatter plot
C) A card
D) A table
notes.choicesExplained: A: a pie shows parts of one total. C: a card shows a single value. D: a table lists values but does not reveal a relationship at a glance.
notes.explanation: Comparing two numeric measures to find a correlation is what scatter plots are for.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Scatter plots”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A finance director wants the top of a report page to show one headline number: this year’s total income. Which visual should the analyst use?
notes.back: A card.
notes.explanation: Cards show individual values, which suits highlighting one important figure.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Tables and text”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: On a report page, a user clicks the Leeds column in a chart of sales by city. What happens to the page’s other related visuals?
notes.back: They automatically filter to Leeds, with Leeds highlighted.
notes.explanation: Visuals for related data in a Power BI report are linked, so a selection in one filters the others.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe considerations for data visualization, “Interactive reports in Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Two teams are building separate reports that must use identical revenue measures and the same table relationships. What should both reports be built on?
notes.back: B: one shared semantic model.
notes.choices:
A) One dashboard
B) One shared semantic model
C) The Power BI mobile app
D) Two separate workspaces
notes.choicesExplained: A: a dashboard displays tiles; reports are not built on it. D: separate workspaces would not make the logic identical. C: the mobile app is for viewing.
notes.explanation: A semantic model defines measures and relationships and can be shared across multiple reports.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Power BI in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Power BI Desktop versus the Power BI service: what is each best for?
notes.back: Desktop: data modelling and report creation. Service: sharing and collaboration.
notes.explanation: Both can connect to data sources and create visualisations.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, What is Power BI?, “Power BI Desktop vs. the Power BI service”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does modelling and report editing in the Power BI service compare with Power BI Desktop?
notes.back: Some basic modelling and editing is possible in the browser, but it is more limited than in Desktop.
notes.explanation: In Fabric, web-based report editing means analysts can now create and update reports without installing Desktop.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe Power BI tools and workflow, “Microsoft Power BI”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Star versus snowflake schema: how do the dimension tables relate?
notes.back: Star: dimension tables relate directly to the fact table. Snowflake: dimension tables also relate to further detail tables.
notes.explanation: The extra detail tables in a snowflake are normalised pieces of a single business entity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Describe core concepts of data modeling, “Tables and schema”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Power BI, which is generally better: mimicking a snowflake dimension, or combining it into one denormalised model table?
notes.back: Generally one model table: its benefits usually outweigh those of several tables.
notes.explanation: The guidance adds that the best choice can depend on data volumes and usability needs.
notes.source: Power BI guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, “Snowflake dimensions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Report versus dashboard in the Power BI service: how do they differ in shape?
notes.back: A report has one or more pages built on one semantic model; a dashboard is a single screen of tiles.
notes.explanation: Dashboards are often used to monitor metrics, while report pages are often organised around specific questions.
notes.source: Power BI documentation, Power BI service basics, “Key Power BI service concepts and terms”
